summary: The migrated WinUI 3 app builds cleanly but cannot be launched. Package registration fails, so no scenario is reachable. Every feature is a FAIL relative to the working UWP original.

discrepancies.detail: Both 'dotnet run' and 'winapp run <build-output>' fail to register the package: error 0x80073CF6 with inner 'error 0x80070002: the system failed to register the windows.capability extension ... The system cannot find the file specified.'
discrepancies.root_cause: Package.appxmanifest declares <uap4:CustomCapability Name="Microsoft.onDemandHotspotControl_8wekyb3d8bbwe" />. A CustomCapability requires a signed custom capability descriptor (SCCD) provisioned on the machine; the sideloaded WinUI 3 package has none, so registration of the windows.capability extension fails and the app never starts.
discrepancies.impact: No UI can be captured or driven; all scenarios/controls are unverifiable and score as FAIL.

discrepancies.detail: The original UWP app launched (ok:true, windowTitle 'OnDemandHotspot C# Sample') and a visual golden was captured, but its CoreWindow exposed no UIA subtree via ApplicationFrameHost, so control-level actuation returned invokeOk:false for all 7 actions. Behavioral baseline is therefore unavailable; scoring relies on build/launch status and the visual golden.
discrepancies.impact: No behavioral regression can be computed, but it is moot because the WinUI app does not launch at all.
